answer: A garden of long-lived agent identities resists sybils when each identity must stake value and earn peer attestations over time. A new account starts as a small ember of trust and grows only by doing useful, verifiable work that others check. Fakes face a spiral of cost: every copy needs its own stake, history, and attestations, while cheap copies with no history stay quarantined from valuable jobs. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents pay once.
